claim: The published surface relationship is recovered under lect renaming, row and column permutation, pair reversal, duplicate lects and principled taxon sampling. Not a claim about inheritance, direction of change or which lect is ancestral.
oracle: Published models are compared as three key sets -- multi-lect classes, per-pair conditioned correspondences and cross-dimensional associations -- with lect ids mapped through the probe's renaming, table and class-id order dropped and decision indices reduced to ranks inside their table.

verdicts.label: same claims and measurements, one environment spelled as an equivalent predicate
verdicts.substantive: the set of published claims changed

probes.claim: renaming without changing the induced order changes nothing at all
renaming so the lect order reverses keeps every published claim
the order of rows in the file is not evidence
which lect is seen first inside a set is not evidence
an identical duplicate lect does not change the pairs it duplicates
missing forms of one lect leave the other lects' pairs alone
an unrelated lect adds pairs without moving the existing ones
writing an affricate apart changes the segmentation, and the relation between the lects has to survive it
a lect bearing existing evidence may change the multi-lect result, and the report has to name the subset
searching both orientations does not manufacture an association where neither has one

gates: order-preserving renaming, row reversal and first-seen reversal change nothing
order-reversing renaming and pair reversal keep every published claim
a duplicate lect leaves the pairs it duplicates alone and is counted as one
missing forms of one lect leave the other lects' pairs alone
an unrelated lect leaves the existing pairs alone
a corpus with no association publishes none in either orientation
real corpora are measured and reported, not gated
